As a Lead Product Manager for Developer Productivity, you will own the product areas developers rely on, and you will own something harder: the end-to-end workflows that determine how productive our engineers actually are. Establish product vision and northstar for your area, and connect it into the broader developer productivity strategy
Own cross-cutting developer workflows end to end — mapping where they break across pillars like App & Cloud Infra, Reliability Engineering, and Developer Experience, and driving the changes that improve them
Define how we measure developer productivity: build the metrics, instrumentation, and qualitative research that tell us whether engineers' lives are actually getting better
Partner with Engineering, Product, TPM, and Data Science to understand goals and establish success criteria with clearly measurable objectives and key results
Develop the product roadmap, and get alignment on prioritization and timelines to meet business goals
Influence teams you don't own — build the case, bring the data, and get other groups to prioritize developer productivity work alongside their own roadmaps
Develop a deep understanding of how Airbnb's engineers work day to day, and of the technical architecture underneath, to build and improve products that fit into real workflows rather than around them
Execute efficiently to ship products and deliver impact for our business and users.
Lead cross-functional groups to fulfill the team’s mission, acting as the system voice.
Communicate concisely and influence outcomes at all levels of the organization, demonstrating strong executive presence.

10+ years of product management experience building tools and platforms for technical users — developer tooling, infrastructure, or platform products
Track record of improving developer or engineering productivity, with the measurements to prove it
Experience defining and operationalizing metrics for hard-to-quantify outcomes — when quantitative metrics are needed and matter, and when qualitative metrics may or may not be more impactful
Strong understanding of technical architecture for complex and highly scalable systems, and of modern AI-powered developer workflows: AI-assisted development, code review, CI/CD, build systems, testing, deployment
Demonstrated ability to drive outcomes across organizational boundaries without direct authority — influencing roadmaps you don't own
Ability to understand immediate and longer-term customer goals and needs, and build products that meet them
Entrepreneurial drive, and demonstrated ability to lead and influence cross-functional teams to align on a vision and product strategy
Ability to quickly absorb technical concepts and communicate effectively with technical and non-technical partners at every level of the organization
Ability to prioritize and scope user requests and platform capabilities, balancing long-term vision against short-term pain points
Previous experience as a software engineer, or working extremely closely with engineering teams, is a strong plus

Key cross-functional partners include Engineering, Procurement, and FP&A, among others.

This role owns the understanding, forecasting, and influencing of Airbnb's total cloud and AI spend, spanning traditional AWS infrastructure and AI. Success looks like a cost narrative leadership can act on, and identified efficiency opportunities that measurably bend the cost curve without degrading product or employee experience. This includes leading planning cycles (FY26 close-out, FY27 guidance) and driving month-over-month rigor in cost variance analysis.
A Typical Day:
Build and maintain the monthly/weekly cloud and AI cost forecast, reconciling actuals against plan and explaining variance drivers to leadership.

Foundational Data sits inside Cloud Infrastructure and is a deliberate mix of Data Engineers and Analytics Engineers working as one team.

Because we are a mixed DE and AE team, you will work across both disciplines: this role needs data engineering depth, plus enough fluency in metric and dimensional modeling to set direction for the analytics engineering side.

The signals describing our fleets are fragmented across cost, utilization telemetry, service performance, and GPU and model telemetry. Nobody has modeled this coherently yet, and the AI side is the least charted part of all. There is no schema to inherit. You would decide what these datasets are, then bring the rest of the company along.
This work carries regular visibility to directors and VPs across Infrastructure and Finance.

Own how Airbnb measures its AI: the unit economics of training and serving our own models, GPU fleet utilization, and the cost and adoption of developer AI tooling
Design and build the datasets that integrate cost, utilization, performance, and reliability signals across Airbnb's infrastructure fleets, starting from a blank page
Stay hands-on in the pipelines and models you architect, close enough to the build to catch the problems design reviews miss
Influence and coach a distributed team of Data Engineers and Analytics Engineers, raising the quality bar through design and code review and scaling it by building the frameworks and automated checks other teams adopt
Navigate conflicting stakeholder requirements across Infrastructure, Finance, Data Science, and Product Engineering, and land a single definition everyone can build on
Identify and eliminate duplication and data fragmentation across the engineering organization, driving deprecation of what your models replace
Participate in the team's on-call rotation for the datasets we own

12+ years of relevant industry experience with a BS/Masters, or 9+ years with a PhD, in data engineering or a closely related field
You have designed, built, and operated production data pipelines at large scale, and you write strong SQL and Python. Scala experience is useful but not required
You can design a dimensional model and define a metric others will trust, even if analytics engineering has not been your job title
You have moved into an unfamiliar data or technical domain and become productive quickly, building enough understanding of the underlying systems to model them well
You have been the technical lead on a team or program, setting direction that other senior engineers executed against without formal authority over them, while still writing code yourself
You have written the multi-year technical strategy for an area, and got other organizations to fund and deliver against it
You have built a data product where no schema or precedent existed, and persuaded other teams to adopt it
You have written the document that aligned several teams on a contested technical decision, and you can explain a data model to a finance partner as readily as to an engineer

Airbnb’s Data Infrastructure organization builds the platforms that power data across the company. Within it, the Data Movement & Transformation (DMT) pillar builds the platform that moves data between Airbnb’s storage engines and transforms it along the way.
Today, data moves through many bespoke, one-off pipelines that are built and maintained differently by each team. We’re replacing them with one unified, declarative platform. You define data once, and it is replicated everywhere it needs to go. This work underpins Airbnb’s Data as a Service initiative.
You’ll join the team that owns three connected layers of that platform:
Control plane: the layer that turns declarative data definitions into running pipelines, including provisioning, runtime selection, and lifecycle management.
Schema: how schemas are defined, tracked, and evolved safely across every system and engine.
Realtime Data Infrastructure (RTDI): Kafka and the streaming transport layer that real-time data flows through at scale.
As a Staff Software Engineer, you’ll set technical direction across these layers and stay hands-on in the code.
Examples of the Difference You’ll Make
Design and evolve the control plane that automatically provisions Kafka topics, registers schemas, and deploys pipelines from a declarative definition.
Build schema management that makes evolution safe and backward compatible across streaming, storage, and warehouse systems.
Improve the reliability, scalability, and cost efficiency of RTDI and Kafka at Airbnb’s scale, including capacity, multi-tenancy, and failure handling.
Replace fragmented pipeline tooling with shared, self-serve platform abstractions that other teams adopt.
Lead design reviews and incident follow-through, and raise the engineering and operational bar for the team.
Your Expertise
9+ years of software engineering, including significant experience building and operating large-scale distributed systems, ideally data platforms, event-driven systems, or streaming infrastructure.
Hands-on experience with Kafka or a similar distributed log or messaging system, with a good understanding of partitioning, delivery semantics, throughput, and operational tradeoffs.
Experience designing schema or data contract systems, such as schema registries, serialization formats like Avro or Protobuf, and compatibility and evolution strategies.
Experience building control planes or platform APIs, such as declarative configuration, reconciliation, workflow orchestration, or resource provisioning, ideally on Kubernetes.
